summary: All active occurrences retain stem II despite mta- shapes and Arabic V ancestry. The inspected ʔxr and wxr entries instead present Detransitive lateness; this input’s t-containing forms and arguments support txr without collapsing related roots.

The new sense 2 is licensed by valency: authorities postpone i daʕwa and soldiers hold a priest back with object -le. The two postponed-hearing tokens are one repeated report, not two independent attestations. Case postponement is not separately numbered as a legal technical meaning.
Active II is regularly intransitive with L-series agents: -le, feminine -la and plural endings. It contrasts with a Part. Pass. predicate for a position already occupied behind someone (29/179).
The Infectum box already exists but is empty. mtaxri m ḥḏoḏe fills it; this is a first example, not discovery of a missing form box.

Imperativ variants mtaxar/mtaxər and taxar/taxər/Taxeru occur with m-sources (from before someone, from sight, from a path). These literal source phrases and conventional step-aside commands do not establish separate idioms.
Aspect: blocked or negated retreat in 65/518 contrasts with possible future reciprocal retreat under balki in 65/527; the Preterit form is retained even where the edition uses narrative nonpast.
Confirm the agent/object segmentation of mtaxarre and mtaxralle in Lahdo Traitor 1/62, especially the resumed feminine case object. Their transitive meaning is supported by the full sentence.

Is court postponement conventional with txr across dialects, and does the active transitive use allow both persons and events without restrictions? The present evidence covers one repeated hearing report and one priest token.
